subject: Order Form: billing ownership, net terms, and tax flow — redline handoff
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Torres <emily.torres@acme.cloud>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form: billing ownership, net terms, and tax flow — redline handoff

Kim / Karthik —

Attaching ACME's latest redlines to the Order Form (attached) and the pricing schedule they provided. Legal asked us to confirm the following items before we push the redline back: 

- Which entity will receive invoices (Redwood US vs Redwood EMEA) and whether Acme requires EU VAT reverse-charge evidence.
- Net terms ask: Acme has requested Net 60 (customer-side procurement). We currently price under Net 30; need legal/finance sign-off for Net 60 and any SLA/credit implications.
- Minimum commit phasing: customer wants to backload Q1 commit into Q4; need to ensure invoicing cadence and cancellation clawback are properly captured.
- Tax responsibility and withholding language: Acme's counsel added a clause that shifts VAT/responsibility to the vendor if they provide tax residency certificates. We need a short playbook for evidence collection.

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_v3.pdf, ACME_Pricing_Schedule.xlsx.

Can you review the attached redlines and call out any commercial concessions we should push back on? If possible, highlight any language we should not accept (entity shift, unilateral tax indemnity, or long net terms without finance guardrails).

I propose a short sync today at 4pm PT if you're available; otherwise I'll collect comments and draft a response.

Thanks —
Nikhil
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ACME_OrderForm_v3.pdf (PDF)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Torres <emily.torres@acme.cloud>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form: billing ownership, net terms, and tax flow — redline handoff

Thanks for the context — quick notes from legal (high level):

1) Entity / invoice recipient: do not accept language that allows Acme to reassign invoice recipient without Redwood's written consent. Proposed counter: fixed remit entity in Order Form; changes require 30-day written notice and PO/COA.

2) Net terms: Net 60 is commercially acceptable only if Finance gets a credit hold and PS/implementation acceptance milestones are aligned. Legal to accept Net 60 provided Sales confirms internal Finance sign-off and SOW milestone triggers any acceleration.

3) Tax & withholding: Customer's proposed vendor-responsibility language is asymmetric. We should require: (a) customer provides valid tax residency certificate within 30 days; (b) Redwood will remit taxes where applicable; (c) an indemnity cap tied to fees for the tax period.

4) Minimum commit phasing/backloading: If they move commit timing, we need explicit invoicing schedule and a pro-rata charge if early termination occurs. Add a paragraph to Order Form Appendix specifying invoice dates per quarter.

I attached a redline (redlines_ACME_OrderForm_v3.docx) with inline suggested language. I can join a 4pm PT sync — will be quick (15–20m).

-Kim
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redlines_ACME_OrderForm_v3.docx (DOCX)]

From: Emily Torres <emily.torres@acme.cloud>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Li <mark.li@acme.cloud>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 11:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: billing ownership, net terms, and tax flow — redline handoff

Hi Nikhil / Kim —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side so the legal teams are aligned: 

- Invoices: Acme prefers a single Redwood global invoice to our main finance entity (Acme Cloud Solutions, LLC) for consolidated reporting. We can provide a PO referencing Redwood US entity.
- Net 60: This is standard for our enterprise deals; we can accept milestone-based holdbacks if needed.
- VAT / withholding: Our tax team will provide residency certificates if required. The proposed indemnity cap sounds reasonable — can you share Redwood's typical cap (e.g., 1x monthly fees or similar)?

We are happy to take the redline and work with your legal team. Would prefer to avoid multiple entity invoicing if possible — it complicates our AP.

Best,
Emily Torres
Head of Finance, Acme Cloud Solutions
[Attachment: ACME_PO_45321.pdf (PDF)]

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@acme.cloud>, Mark Li <mark.li@acme.cloud>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: billing ownership, net terms, and tax flow — redline handoff

Emily / Mark —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick operational plan to keep things moving: 

1) Invoicing entity: Redwood can bill a single Redwood US entity for this deal. Kim and Finance will add standard language to protect Redwood if Acme later requests an entity re-assignment.
2) Net terms: I will loop in Finance to confirm Net 60 acceptance with the following guardrails: credit check, milestone acceptance, and a 30-day payment reserve for the first invoice cycle. Karthik — can you confirm Finance is OK to proceed with Net 60 under those conditions?
3) VAT/residency: Emily — please share the residency certificate when available. Kim will include the indemnity cap proposal in her redline.
4) Commit phasing: I propose we accept their backload request if the Order Form Appendix lists explicit invoice dates and an early-termination pro-rata.

Next steps: Kim to send final redline by EOD; Karthik to confirm Finance guardrails; Emily to share residency docs and confirm PO remittance details. If anyone needs to escalate on Net terms, flag to me and I will route to Revenue Ops.

Thanks —
Nikhil
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ACME_Pricing_Schedule.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Torres <emily.torres@acme.cloud>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: billing ownership, net terms, and tax flow — redline handoff

Nikhil / Kim / Emily —

Finance confirms we can move to Net 60 for Acme subject to the following: 

- Completed credit check (internal) with no red flags.
- First invoice will include a 30-day payment reserve hold to cover unexpected disputes — this will be released after the first two on-time payments.
- Any invoice > $250k requires pre-notification to Revenue Ops.

Kim — please include the Net 60 acceptance language and the hold-release condition in the redline. Emily — once you provide the residency certificate and PO, we can finalize the invoice recipient.

I'll mark this as ready for Legal redline finalization after Kim updates the doc.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
